title: CHAPTER 3: CONTRACT LAW — INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 governs the formation, validity, and enforcement of contracts in India.
Key legal concepts include Essentials of a Valid Contract, Discharge of Contract, and Remedies for Breach.
Indemnity and Guarantee are special contracts governed under Sections 124–147.
Bailment and Pledge constitute special bailment arrangements under Sections 148–181.
Agency law defines principal-agent relationships under Sections 182–238.

blocks.content: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 governs contracts in India. A contract is an agreement enforceable by law. Every promise and every set of promises forming consideration for each other is an agreement. An agreement that is enforceable by law is a contract.

cells: Expression of willingness to do or abstain from doing something with a view to obtaining the assent of another
When person to whom offer is made signifies assent thereto; must be absolute and unqualified
Something done, abstained, or promised in return for promise; 'quid pro quo'; past consideration valid in India
Major (18 years); of sound mind; not disqualified by law; minor's contract is void ab initio (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose, 1903)
Consent free from coercion (15), undue influence (16), fraud (17), misrepresentation (18), mistake (20–22)
Object must be legal; not contrary to law, immoral, or opposed to public policy
Agreement not declared void by any law (wagering contracts, agreements in restraint of trade, etc.)
Not enforceable from the very beginning; no legal effect
Agreement with minor; agreement in restraint of marriage; wagering agreement
Valid when formed; subsequently becomes void due to some event
Agreement with alien enemy after war declared; frustration of contract
Enforceable at the option of one party; other party cannot enforce
Contract obtained by coercion, fraud, misrepresentation — aggrieved party may avoid
Valid but cannot be enforced due to technical defect
Oral contract required to be in writing; time-barred contract
Against law; no civil remedy; collateral transactions also void
Contract to commit crime; contract against public policy
Actual performance (complete) or attempted performance (tender of performance)
Novation (new contract replacing old), Rescission (mutual cancellation), Alteration, Remission, Waiver
Section 56: subsequent impossibility due to supervening events (death, destruction, law change, frustration of purpose)
Death, insolvency, merger, lapse of time (Limitation Act bars remedy, not right)
Actual breach (at time of performance) or Anticipatory breach (before performance date)
Compensation for loss; ordinary damages (natural consequences); special damages (Hadley v. Baxendale rule); nominal damages; liquidated damages vs penalty
Court orders defaulting party to perform the contract; discretionary; granted where damages inadequate (e.g., unique property)
Court restrains party from doing something; temporary, permanent, or mandatory injunction
Reasonable compensation for work done when contract becomes void or one party prevented from completing
Cancellation of contract; puts parties in original position; restoration of benefits
Section 124: Promise by one party (indemnifier) to save another (indemnified/indemnity-holder) from loss caused by promisor's conduct or any other person's conduct
Section 126: Contract to perform the promise, or discharge liability of a third person in case of default; principal debtor must exist
Three parties; secondary liability; co-extensive with principal debtor
Co-extensive with principal debtor; surety liable to same extent as principal debtor unless otherwise provided
Surety can revoke continuing guarantee for future transactions by notice
Variance in terms; release of principal debtor; loss of security; act of omission by creditor impairing surety's rights
Right of subrogation (stand in creditor's shoes); right to indemnity from principal debtor; right to share in securities held by creditor

items: Match the specific section ranges: Indemnity/Guarantee (Sec. 124–147), Bailment/Pledge (Sec. 148–181), and Agency (Sec. 182–238).
Pay special attention to the legal distinctions between Void and Voidable contracts as well as specific remedies for breach of contract.

cells: Delivery of goods for some purpose; returned or disposed as per directions after purpose accomplished; bailment of services not covered (Ultramares)
Bailor = person delivering goods; Bailee = person receiving goods on bailment
Standard of 'reasonable man' — not absolute; negligence standard
No reward; bailor liable only for known defects; bailee liable for gross negligence
For reward; bailor liable even for unknown defects; bailee liable for negligence
Bailment of goods as security for payment of debt or performance of promise; Pawnor = pledgor; Pawnee = pledgee
Right to sue pawnor for debt, to sell goods after reasonable notice; right to retain goods till payment
Has duties of a bailee; can sue for specific reward if promised; can sell perishable goods
Agent = person employed to do act for another or represent another in dealings with third persons; Principal = person for whom agent acts
By express agreement, implied conduct, ratification, necessity, estoppel; consideration not necessary
Authority that third parties reasonably believe agent has even if not actually conferred; principal bound
Principal can ratify unauthorised act of agent; retrospective effect; cannot ratify partly; must ratify whole
Follow principal's instructions; conduct business with reasonable skill; render accounts; communicate; not to make secret profit; not to delegate (delegatus non potest delegare)
Right to remuneration; right to lien on goods and papers; right of indemnity and compensation
By revocation by principal; by renunciation by agent; completion of business; death/insanity/insolvency of principal or agent; destruction of subject matter
Agency where agent has interest in subject matter; cannot be revoked without express consent; e.g., agent authorised to sell goods and pay himself from proceeds
